title: Seoul eats: 13 spots from classics to burgers
desc: Seoul restaurants grouped into Korean classics, noodles and dumplings, chicken and BBQ, and burgers.

items.title: Tosokchon Samgyetang (토속촌 삼계탕)
items.memo: Ginseng chicken soup in a hanok near Gyeongbokgung, served with ginseng wine.

items.title: Ikseon Tonkatsu (익선돈가스)
items.memo: Big, tender Korean-style pork cutlets with curry sauce.

items.title: Yeongchunok (영춘옥)
items.memo: 75+ years old; gomtang with a rich, milky beef bone broth.

items.title: Gwangjang Market (광장시장)
items.memo: Market from 1905; go for crispy mung bean bindaetteok.

items.title: Gossine Donghae Makguksu, Jongno (고씨네동해막국수 종로직영점)
items.memo: Hanok-style spot for bibimbap and cold buckwheat noodles.

items.title: Bangtae Makguksu (방태막국수)
items.memo: Bibim and mul makguksu, plus bossam pork belly.

items.title: Bukchon Son-mandu, Samcheong-dong (북촌손만두 삼청동)
items.memo: Steamed and fried mandu platters and mandu soup near Bukchon.

items.title: Myeongdong Kyoja (명동교자 본점)
items.memo: 50+ years, four-item menu: kalguksu and steamed mandu.

items.title: Art Monster Ikseon-dong (아트몬스터 익선동)
items.memo: Cozy chimaek: double-fried chicken with craft beer.

items.title: Anguk Restaurant Doma (도마)
items.memo: Mostly Korean BBQ; the yuzu ramen is a standout.

items.title: Smoke Town (스모크타운)
items.memo: American BBQ platters, brisket and pulled pork, with robot waiters.
